title: Keel Beam — Bolted Splice Repair of a Cracked Stiffener at the Centre Wing Box Junction
abstract: Bolted splice repair of a cracked keel beam stiffener at the centre wing box junction, used after a crack is found during a scheduled inspection of the belly fairing area.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the load path across a cracked keel beam stiffener at the centre wing box junction by installing a bolted splice, without removing the keel beam.
sections.damage_assessment: Remove the belly fairing panels and clean the stiffener over the full length of the affected bay. Establish both crack tips by high frequency eddy current and confirm them by dye penetrant. Record the crack length and its position relative to the junction fitting. A crack that has reached the junction fitting land, a crack in the beam web rather than the stiffener, or a crack accompanied by corrosion in the same bay is outside the scope of this repair. Inspect the plate VER592606-06 and the cleat D5322127693175 at the same station for secondary indications, and inspect the drainage path in the bay; standing water in the keel beam bay is a common contributor and it must be reported with the finding.
sections.repair_procedure: Drill and ream the crack stop holes at both tips to the diameter on repair drawing RD-53-22-12-916 and confirm by dye penetrant that the tips are captured. Machine the splice seat on the stiffener flange and prepare the faying surfaces. Apply the chromate-free protection to all bare material including the crack stop holes. Fit the splice plate GIR790257-43 dry and check the fit with a feeler gauge, shimming any gap larger than the drawing value. Install the anchor nuts AGS116381-2C in the stiffener flange to the pattern on sheet 2. Install the fasteners wet with sealant, working outwards from the crack stop positions, using the titanium bolts AGS631240K7 at the six positions nearest the junction fitting. Torque the fasteners in the sequence on sheet 3. Seal the splice edge, re-establish the drainage path and restore the protection scheme before the fairing is refitted.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a high frequency eddy current inspection of both crack stop holes and of the splice perimeter every 4000 flight cycles, with the belly fairing panels removed. Do a detailed visual inspection of the bay drainage at every A check. Any growth from a crack stop hole, any indication at the junction fitting land, or standing water in the bay makes the repair invalid pending an engineering assessment. The repair is life limited to 12000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: A single crack up to 40 millimetres in the stiffener flange, not reaching the junction fitting land, not in the beam web and with no corrosion in the same bay.

repair_drawings.title: Bolted splice, keel beam stiffener at centre wing box junction

type_data.fastener_pattern: Three rows, 40 fasteners, 24 mm pitch, 18 mm edge distance, with the centre row staggered across the stiffener flange
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 12000 flight cycles; a repeat high frequency eddy current inspection is required every 4000 flight cycles.
type_data.aerodynamic_smoothness: Not applicable, covered by the belly fairing
